facts.text: The male superb fairywren in breeding plumage glows with a bright blue forehead, ear coverts, mantle and tail, set off by a black throat and mask.
facts.quote: the male in breeding plumage has a striking bright blue forehead, ear coverts, mantle, and tail, with a black mask and black or dark blue throat.

facts.text: The superb fairywren's blue plumage reflects ultraviolet light strongly, so it may look even more vivid to other fairywrens, whose vision extends into ultraviolet.
facts.quote: The blue plumage also reflects ultraviolet light strongly, and so may be even more prominent to other fairywrens, whose colour vision extends into this part of the spectrum.

facts.text: Superb fairywrens are socially monogamous but sexually promiscuous: pairs bond for life while both partners regularly mate with other individuals.
facts.quote: Fairywrens are socially monogamous and sexually promiscuous: pairs will bond for life, though both males and females will regularly mate with other individuals

facts.text: Superb fairywrens teach their chicks a vocal 'password' before hatching, helping them avoid being tricked by cuckoo parasites.
facts.quote: The bird appears to also use vocalisations as a password for its chicks to give it a chance to avoid cuckoo parasites.

facts.text: Groups of three to five superb fairywrens defend small territories year-round, with helper birds feeding and rearing the young.
facts.quote: The superb fairywren is a cooperative breeding species, with pairs or groups of 3–5 birds maintaining and defending small territories year-round.

facts.text: The superb fairywren thrives in cities and gardens and was voted Australian Bird of the Year for 2021, narrowly beating the tawny frogmouth by 666 votes.
facts.quote: The superb fairywren was named 'Australian Bird of the Year' for 2021, after a survey conducted by Birdlife Australia saw the species narrowly defeat the tawny frogmouth with a margin of 666 votes

facts.text: During the reproductive season, male superb fairywrens pluck yellow petals, which contrast with their plumage, and show them to female fairywrens.
facts.quote: During the reproductive season, males of this and other fairywren species pluck yellow petals, which contrast with their plumage, and show them to female fairywrens.

facts.text: The superb fairywren may use a 'rodent-run' display to distract predators from nests with young birds.
facts.quote: Superb fairywrens may utilise a 'rodent-run' display to distract predators from nests with young birds.

facts.text: Male superb fairywrens have a peculiar song-like vocalization given in response to the calls of predatory birds, commonly grey butcherbirds.
facts.quote: Males also possess a peculiar song-like Type II vocalization, which is given in response to the calls of predatory birds, commonly grey butcherbirds.

facts.text: Superb fairywren eggs are incubated for 14 days, after which they hatch within 24 hours.
facts.quote: The eggs are incubated for 14 days, after which they hatch within 24 hours.
